_what: Citation anchor for the biomarker-selected-classes paper. Every identifier the manuscript prints appears here, and every record here was READ OUT OF A RETRIEVED EUROPE PMC PAYLOAD in this session — never recalled, never copied from a review.
⛔_why_this_file_exists: CLAUDE.md §7: an agent drafting a manuscript once wrote a PMID from recollection that existed in no committed source in this repository, and it passed the language linter twice because claim STRENGTH is orthogonal to citation PROVENANCE. lint_citations.py asks the one question an offline checker can answer — does this identifier also appear in a tracked .json, i.e. in a fetch product. This is that fetch product.
⚠_what_anchoring_does_not_mean: An anchored identifier is NOT thereby verified. This file is evidence that a retrieval returned these records with these titles and authors. It is not evidence that the papers say what the manuscript says they say — only reading them is, and for each record below the reason it is cited is stated so a reviewer can check that specific claim rather than the citation as a whole.
_not_medical_advice: ⛔ Nothing here asserts efficacy, safety, a therapeutic window or clinical readiness for any agent in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma. These are class-definition references: they establish what biomarker each therapeutic class is SELECTED ON, which is the question the manuscript asks of public expression data.

retrieval.route: workflow_dispatch of .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml at ref=claude/cancer-treatment-emc-categories-nu4nfd via the `targets_json` inline manifest
retrieval.why_ci: this sandbox's egress proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for www.ebi.ac.uk (CLAUDE.md §6)
retrieval.api: Europe PMC REST search, resultType=core, sort=CITED desc
retrieval.⚠_a_first_attempt_returned_the_wrong_thi: An earlier dispatch (slug biomarker-class-definitions-2026-08-09) used unsorted relevance queries and returned recent reviews rather than the class-defining papers, and one query returned hitCount 0. Its records were NOT used. Citing from that list would have meant attributing a class definition to a paper nobody had read, which is the exact failure this file exists to prevent.

_anchor_form: Each record carries `pubmed_url`, which is the form lint_citations reads. ⚠ A bare `pmid` field is deliberately NOT an anchor form — a bare-digit rule could falsely anchor a fabricated identifier colliding with an unrelated number, which is the one direction that gate must never move. The DOIs anchor on their own pattern.
